text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc's chief executive Derek Wanless on Thursday stressed his confidence in Martin Owen, head of NatWest's investment bank.

Earlier the British banking group said Owen, chief executive of NatWest Markets, would forego part of his 1996 bonus following revelations of a 90 million pound ($143.7 million) loss in interest rate options.
Wanless told Reuters in a telephone interview that he had complete confidence in Owen, who will give up 200,000 pounds of a 500,000 pound bonus.
"It is a set-back for Martin in one area. We'll learn a lot from it, get those lessons put into practice and that will make us much stronger," Wanless said.
NatWest published the early findings of a probe into the options losses on Thursday, less than two weeks after revealing what were initially put at losses of 50 million pounds.
The bank said the losses, dating back to 1994, were the result of mispricing and would result in a charge of 77 million pound provision against pre-tax profits for the first half of 1997.

NatWest said it had already made provisions of five million pounds and a further eight million would be clawed back through bonuses which would not now be paid to certain employees in its global debt derivatives division. ($ = 0.626 British Pounds)
